purpose: Wire these into the harness's lifecycle hooks so the checkpoint triggers the harness owns fire without relying on the agent (CHECKPOINT_POLICY.mandatory_triggers: {{checkpoint_triggers}}). The watchdog (gov checkpoint watchdog) and the boundary observer still checkpoint any trigger a harness cannot hook, at the next execution boundary.

environment.GOV_ROLE: the acting role the harness declared for the session (L1 or above: checkpoint authority)
environment.GOV_SESSION: the session id the harness declared

hooks.when: immediately before the harness compacts or truncates the model context
command: resume after context compaction: run gov status, then gov continue
hooks.shell: gov checkpoint create --trigger before_compaction --next-action 'resume after context compaction: run gov status, then gov continue'

hooks.when: when the agent session ends (normally or on interruption)
before the harness switches the model or provider serving the session
command: resume on the new model: run gov status, then gov continue
hooks.shell: gov checkpoint create --trigger before_model_switch --next-action 'resume on the new model: run gov status, then gov continue'

on_failure: A hook command that fails is reported by the harness and never blocks the human; gov session close is never refused (it states its degradation), and a refused checkpoint names its cause (e.g. AUTHORITY_DENIED for an undeclared role).
